description: Shop-floor process vocabulary: operations, QC gates, holds, rework and scrap.

receipt.description: Material or a work order arrives and the flow begins.

material_issue.description: Pull or issue material from inventory against the order.

lot_capture.description: Record lot or serial numbers so the unit stays traceable.

operation.description: A routing operation performed at a work centre (mill, cure, assemble).

inspection.description: A QC gate. Always has both a pass and a fail path.

rework.description: Corrective work on a failed unit before it re-enters the flow.

hold.description: The unit is parked pending a disposition decision.

move.description: Transfer between work centres or storage locations.

label_print.description: Call out to a printer, scanner, scale or other shop-floor system.

scrap.description: The unit leaves the flow as scrap.

ship.description: The unit is completed and leaves as good product.

elicitation: What kicks the order off — material arriving, or a released work order?
What are the routing operations, in order, and which work centre does each?
On a fail, does the unit rework, go on hold for a disposition, or get scrapped?
If it reworks, which operation does it go back to?
Where are lot or serial numbers captured?
How does a good unit leave the flow?
